translations.source_sense_description: aufdonnern, tunen, etwas übertrieben zurechtmachen, herrichten oder aufrüsten

glosses: Someone who solicits customers for prostitution and acts as manager for a group of prostitutes; a pander.

examples.text: A fella looking dapper / And he's sittin' with a slapper / Then I see it's a pimp / And his crack whore
All my life, been hustling / And tonight is my appraisal / 'Cause I'm a hooker selling songs / And my pimp's a record label

glosses: A man who can easily attract women.
To act as a procurer of prostitutes; to pander.
To prostitute someone.

examples.text: The smooth-talking, tall man with heavy gold bracelets claimed he could pimp anyone.

glosses: To excessively customize something, especially a vehicle.

examples.text: You pimped out that motorcycle f'real, dawg.

glosses: To ask progressively harder and ultimately unanswerable questions of a resident or medical student (said of a senior member of the medical staff).

examples.text: Only an attending physician can pimp a chief resident; the chief resident and attending can pimp a junior resident; they all three can pimp an intern.

glosses: To promote, to tout.

examples.text: I gotta show you this sweet website where you can pimp your blog and get more readers.
The trendy rehabs being pimped by the addiction industry's glossy PR.

glosses: To persuade, smooth talk or trick another into doing something for your benefit.

examples.text: I pimped her out of $2,000 and she paid for the entire stay at the Bahamas.

glosses: Excellent, fashionable, stylish.
Five in Cumbrian and Welsh sheep counting.

translations.source_sense_description: aufdonnern, tunen, etwas übertrieben zurechtmachen, herrichten oder aufrüsten

glosses: To modify the engine of (a motor vehicle) to give a higher performance than the specifications.

examples.text: Imagine souping up a Mini with a Cosworth engine: the car would fly.

glosses: To embellish with many additions.

examples.text: They are dickering over a tax cut small enough, in a bill "souped" up with gadgets, to escape or override a veto.

translations.source_sense_description: aufdonnern, tunen, etwas übertrieben zurechtmachen, herrichten oder aufrüsten

glosses: To make adjustments (to an engine or bicycle drivetrain) in order to improve its performance.
To make preparations for vigorous exercise; to warm up.
To begin to sing or play music.
To tune one's instrument in preparation for performance.
To beat up (someone).

examples.text:
“We finally stopped roustin' him and decided to tune him up instead, every chance we got.”
“Tune him up?”
“Yeah, that's an expression for beatin' the living dog shit outta somebody.”
“I mean, I had to tune her up a bit. She bitched a lot and never did any work. Sometimes, you know, you just gotta get their attention, whack 'em a little."
[T]hey couldn't tune him up because the murder had to look like he died in his sleep.
